newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds end lower after rate decision.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds end lower after rate decision.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed lower across the board on Tuesday following the Bank of Israel's decision to leave interest rates unchanged, traders said.
On Monday, after the market close, the central bank said it would hold its key lending rate for December at an annualised 15.2 percent.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon - issued for four years): -0.1 pct to 170.33.
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: -0.02 pct to 160.91
Volume was low at 137 million shekels with dollar-linked bonds falling sharply following the shekel's rise against the dollar.

"Overall the reaction to the interest rate decision was very moderate and the fall in bond prices was below expectations. The mild decline in unlinked bonds came as a real surprise," said Ron Weisberg of IBI Investment House.
Traders noted that on Monday analysts had started lowering their rate-cut forecasts to 0.3 percentage point or less.
Uri Schur of Eyal Securities said the drop in CPI bond prices was only indirectly connected with the interest rate news.

"Prices of CPI-linked long bonds fell today because of profit-taking," he said. "Yields on inflation-linked bonds had been falling over the last four months from 5.3 percent to less than 4.5 percent. The rate decision was only a trigger."

The unlinked segment also weathered the rate news well. "The main reason for the decline in the unlinked bonds was (unfulfilled) expectations for a minimal rate cut," said Weisberg. "Despite that, the reaction was very moderate. The mild decline of the Makam was a real surprise."
Dollar-linked bonds were the biggest losers. "Investors were reacting to the rise of the shekel on Monday immediately following the rate announcement", Schur said.
On Tuesday, the representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.2420 shekels against 3.2470 on Monday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
